title: Priority Signal Harmonizer — tiered intake, SLA escalations, and commitment ledger
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: top accounts and enterprise customers submit high-signal requests that are currently handled in ad-hoc threads, resulting in unclear SLAs, duplicated intake, and inconsistent priority decisions. This ticket defines a small scoped program to harmonize signals across sales/CS/engineering, introduce tiered intake forms, and codify an escalation + commitment ledger so PMs can make consistent, auditable roadmap commitments to VIP customers.

Approach: 1) Define a short canonical intake form and mapping of signals (revenue, legal/regulatory, retention risk, strategic bet). 2) Create a prioritization heuristic that maps signal vectors to three intake tiers (Inform, Review, Fast-Track) and associated SLA windows. 3) Surface the ledger and triage state in the PM console view and an on-call escalation runbook for Engineering leads. 4) Pilot with 6 strategic accounts and iterate on scoring weights based on cross-functional feedback.
background: We have many existing PM playbooks (fastpass, priority gates) but no single source of truth that connects customer signals to a deterministic roadmap decision and a visible commitment record. Sales and CS escalate differently; engineering needs clear, time-boxed requests with known acceptance criteria. This creates downstream rework and surprised customers when commitments slip.
scope: Design and publish canonical intake form in Confluence and CS playbook
Implement server-side intake webhook and lightweight scoring service (backend contract only, no heavy infra)
Add a "VIP Intake" tab to the PM roadmap console that shows ledger entries and SLA state
Create escalation runbook templates and on-call notification hooks for Fast-Track items
out_of_scope: Full automation of score weighting via ML (manual weighting for pilot)
Dedicated SLA-backed contractual commits (legal negotiation) — this is operational tooling only
Major UX redesign of Console — add tab/panels only
success_metrics: Mean response time to 'Fast-Track' intake < 48 hours during pilot
>85% of pilot ledger entries have an assigned PM, engineering owner, and target release window
Reduction in cross-functional follow-up threads about scope by 60% for pilot accounts (measured in CS ticket counts)

risks: Scoring weights lead to surprising prioritization; mitigate with stakeholder sign-off and shadow-mode scoring for first 2 weeks
Engineering capacity for Fast-Track items could be insufficient — include explicit capacity guardrails and fallback policy
Visibility gaps between Sales and PMs could persist if ledger is not integrated into CS workflow
acceptance_criteria: Canonical intake form published with field definitions and examples
Scoring service implements the rubric and exposes an API that returns tier and SLA window
Console displays ledger rows with status (Submitted, Under Review, Committed, Delivered) and links to related Jira/PRs
Escalation runbook documented and exercised in one simulated escalation drill involving PM/Eng/CS
Pilot launched with at least 6 accounts and initial metrics dashboard capturing response times and assignment coverage
